MUS 1004.title: School of Performing Arts First Year Experience
MUS 1004.description: Orientation to the School of Performing Arts philosophy and the resources of the School, the College, and the University. Cultivate a common intellectual, analytical, and creative conversation among first-year students. Enhance student participation in the creative and scholarly life of the Schools programs. Foster a sense of community and understanding across disciplines.

MUS 1005.title: Theory Fundamentals
MUS 1005.description: Fundamental elements of music theory. 1005: Introduction to elements of music theory. Musical notation, scales of various global traditions, foundations of tonality; intervals, triads, dominant seventh chords, rhythm, meter, cadences, harmonic analysis. Composition with species counterpoint and the twelve-bar blues progression. Aural recognition of musical sounds through ear training. 1006: More complex harmonic and rhythmic processes. Increase complexity of intervals, chords, rhythms, progressions and score reading. Introduce transposition and vocabulary for timbre and textural discussion. Aural recognition of more advanced musical sounds through ear training. Fluency in terms and conventions for western art music, rock, hip-hop. Composition of original music.

MUS 1006.title: Theory Fundamentals
MUS 1006.description: Fundamental elements of music theory. 1005: Introduction to elements of music theory. Musical notation, scales of various global traditions, foundations of tonality; intervals, triads, dominant seventh chords, rhythm, meter, cadences, harmonic analysis. Composition with species counterpoint and the twelve-bar blues progression. Aural recognition of musical sounds through ear training. 1006: More complex harmonic and rhythmic processes. Increase complexity of intervals, chords, rhythms, progressions and score reading. Introduce transposition and vocabulary for timbre and textural discussion. Aural recognition of more advanced musical sounds through ear training. Fluency in terms and conventions for western art music, rock, hip-hop. Composition of original music.

MUS 1024.title: Music, Wellness, and Healing Arts Traditions
MUS 1024.description: Study global healing traditions through creative, non-performance engagement with music, meditation, movement, and artistic practices. Explore mindfulness and wellness traditions from diverse cultures through listening, guided movement, reflection, and creative exploration rather than performance. Develop personal creative habits that promote stress reduction, focus, and resilience. Cultivate mindful, sustainable practices that support lifelong health, balance, and well-being. No musical training required.

MUS 1104.title: Music Appreciation
MUS 1104.description: Survey of the art of music encompassing a variety of music styles and historical eras in both the western and non- western world. Students will develop strategies to contextualize music, via listening, from the perspective of the listener, composer, and performer.

MUS 1114.title: Listening in the Digital Age
MUS 1114.description: An introduction to musical access and listening in the digital age. Introduces basic elements of music and the creative process together with important musicians and their works. Explores historical, social, and cultural forces and trends that influence the creation and interpretation of various musical styles, including classical, blues, jazz, popular, and world music.

MUS 1124.title: Living a Musical Life
MUS 1124.description: Embrace a wide variety of music and ways to make music. Learn about the health benefits of lifelong music-making. Units include regional, national, and international traditions in historical, political, and cultural contexts. No prior musical training required.

MUS 1134.title: Music of the Americas
MUS 1134.description: Musical traditions in the American continent, with a specific focus on Latin-American and Latinx musics. Introduction to music from different traditions across nations and social-historical contexts. Critical engagement with broad social concepts from cultural, political, and historical perspectives. Development of listening and writing skills.

MUS 1144.title: Topics in Contemporary Pop Music
MUS 1144.description: Examine popular music in cultural, political, and historical perspectives. Introduction to the study of music and its cultural contexts. Technical analysis of music and critical engagement with sociohistorical concepts. Development of listening and writing skills. Course may be repeated once for a maximum of 6 credit hours.

MUS 1154.title: Discover Your Voice
MUS 1154.description: Vocal class for non-music majors, no previous musical experience or audition needed. Develop tools, body awareness, and a daily routine for healthy singing, using your natural speaking voice. Interpret multiple viewpoints of songwriters and learn to communicate the poetry of their music effectively. Analyze songs more deeply from the inside out using the basic building blocks of music theory. Grow more confident to share your voice through music. Reflect on your gradual journey as a developing singer, and how connecting with music impacts your life, mental health, and relationships with others.

MUS 1164.title: Movie Music
MUS 1164.description: Introduction and survey of movie music and its role in narrative film across historical, cultural, and artistic contexts. Students will identify key figures and trends, analyze musical elements and film cues, and evaluate the role of music in cinematic storytelling. Students develop listening and writing skills through engagement with full-length films, film scenes, and their scores.

MUS 1294.title: Guitar 101
MUS 1294.description: Group instruction for beginning and early-stage guitar students focusing on the development of foundational technique, music reading, and chord vocabulary. Develop understanding of a range of beginner-level repertoire and strumming patterns across multiple styles. Emphasis on building functional playing ability, rhythmic accuracy, and ensemble awareness in a collaborative classroom setting. Strengthen musical confidence through guided practice, peer interaction, and skill-based exercises.

MUS 2014.title: AI in Music
MUS 2014.description: Introductory course covers ethical, theoretical, and practical aspects of AI in music. Covers the mechanics of AI and Machine Learning, and the (co-)creation and production of music-centric artifacts using AI tools.

MUS 2025.title: European-American Music Theory
MUS 2025.description: Fundamental elements of music and conventions of genre and style in a global context. 2025: pitch & harmony, rhythm & meter, timbre, texture, and movement. Emphasis on rote learning of pitch notation, intervals, key signatures, chords vs non-chord tones, and pitch collections. Methods to analyze harmony, phrase structure, and meter. Develop vocabulary for timbre and texture. Basic skills of score reading and transposition. 2026: form, as well as more complex harmonic and rhythmic processes, such as harmonic rhythm, syntax and metric dissonance. Increase complexity of score reading to include larger ensembles. In-depth study of genre, considering elements of harmony, rhythm & meter, and form in European and North-American classical, jazz, and popular musics.

MUS 2026.title: European-American Music Theory
MUS 2026.description: Fundamental elements of music and conventions of genre and style in a global context. 2025: pitch & harmony, rhythm & meter, timbre, texture, and movement. Emphasis on rote learning of pitch notation, intervals, key signatures, chords vs non-chord tones, and pitch collections. Methods to analyze harmony, phrase structure, and meter. Develop vocabulary for timbre and texture. Basic skills of score reading and transposition. 2026: form, as well as more complex harmonic and rhythmic processes, such as harmonic rhythm, syntax and metric dissonance. Increase complexity of score reading to include larger ensembles. In-depth study of genre, considering elements of harmony, rhythm & meter, and form in European and North-American classical, jazz, and popular musics.

MUS 2045.title: Sightsinging Laboratory
MUS 2045.description: Study and practice of techniques involved in the sight reading and sightsinging of printed music. Majors and minors only.

MUS 2046.title: Sightsinging Laboratory
MUS 2046.description: Study and practice of techniques involved in the sight reading and sightsinging of printed music. Majors and minors only.

MUS 2054.title: Introduction to Music Technology
MUS 2054.description: History, theory, and applications of music technology. Techniques for notating music and for recording and editing audio, using computer software and digital audio equipment. Consent Required. Design lab.

MUS 2055.title: Audio Technology For Music
MUS 2055.description: Develops basic understanding of audio technology for musical applications, focusing on todays digital audio recording and editing technologies including microphone use, live recording, and studio session recording. Develops critical listening skills through lab experimentation and recording. Pre: Permission of instructor required.

MUS 2056.title: Audio Technology For Music
MUS 2056.description: Develops basic understanding of audio technology for musical applications, focusing on todays digital audio recording and editing technologies including microphone use, live recording, and studio session recording. Develops critical listening skills through lab experimentation and recording. Pre: 2054 and permission of instructor required.

MUS 2065.title: Music Composition
MUS 2065.description: Organizing the basic elements of music: pitch, rhythm, timbre, articulation, and dynamics. Composing pieces for solo instruments and duos. Preparing scores and parts, for performances and recordings of the compositions. Knowledge of basic music theory required. Consent Required.

MUS 2066.title: Music Composition
MUS 2066.description: Composing for specific instruments and combinations of instruments. Exploring traditional and extended technique. Organizing the structure of a piece based on recurrence, development, variation, priority, and perspective of musical material, for trio adn quartet or a larger ensemble. A grade of C or better in prerequisite.

MUS 2074.title: Pro Tools Fundamentals
MUS 2074.description: Introduces the fundamentals of the Avid Pro Tools digital audio workstation (DAW) software, the industry standard for music recording and production, audio for post-production, and more. Differentiates common practices in music recording and production from audio for post production. Provides basic competency in Avid Pro Tools for creating, recording, and mixing music, with a focus on the fundamental skills needed to produce and deliver completed works for mastering, direct distribution, and archival preservation. Includes examination opportunities for Avid Pro Tools user certification. Open to all majors and minors.

MUS 2115.title: Survey of Western Music
MUS 2115.description: Survey and study of the historical evolution of Western art music. MUS 2115: classical music from Antiquity into the Classical era. MUS 2116: classical and other music from the Romantic era through the 20th century to music of today. Investigation of the materials of music. Exploration of music as it both reflects and impacts history, including historical considerations of gender, race, culture, and other extramusical factors. Relevance of historical and contemporary music to our society today.

MUS 2116.title: Survey of Western Music
MUS 2116.description: Survey and study of the historical evolution of Western art music. MUS 2115: classical music from Antiquity into the Classical era. MUS 2116: classical and other music from the Romantic era through the 20th century to music of today. Investigation of the materials of music. Exploration of music as it both reflects and impacts history, including historical considerations of gender, race, culture, and other extramusical factors. Relevance of historical and contemporary music to our society today.

MUS 2124.title: Music Traditions in Appalachia
MUS 2124.description: Survey and study of music traditions in Appalachia. Investigation of the formal elements of this music, including instruments and musical terms and forms. Exploration of style as a reflection of many cultural influences. Study of the impact and development of these traditions in contemporary musical practices.

MUS 2134.title: Disability Culture & the Arts
MUS 2134.description: Disability as an identity, community, and culture through a study of music and the arts. Overview of the disability rights and disability justice movements in the United States, as told through music, film, literature, and performance art. Analyze creative works, confront obstacles to inclusion, and discover disability cultural values. No previous musical training required.

MUS 2144.title: Music and Video Games: History, Aesthetics, Analysis
MUS 2144.description: Introduction to the study of music, games, and audiovisual media and relevant analytical concepts. Intersection of music and video games from historical, aesthetic, and social perspectives. Analysis of video games from musical and ludic perspectives. Development of listening and writing skills.

MUS 2214.title: Class Applied Piano
MUS 2214.description: Group piano lessons for beginners or for students at an early stage of keyboard development. May be repeated for 1 credit. Consent required.

MUS 2224.title: Class Applied Voice
MUS 2224.description: Group voice lessons for beginners or for students at an early stage of vocal development. May be repeated for 1 credit. Consent required.

MUS 2234.title: Class Applied Strings
MUS 2234.description: Group string lessons for beginners or for students at an early stage of string development. May be repeated for 1 credit. Consent required.

MUS 2244.title: Class Applied Woodwinds
MUS 2244.description: Group woodwind lessons for beginners or for students at an early stage of woodwind development. May be repeated for 1 credit. Consent required.

MUS 2254.title: Class Applied Brass
MUS 2254.description: Group brass lessons for beginners or for students at an early stage of brass development. May be repeated for 1 credit. Consent required.

MUS 2264.title: Class Applied Percussion
MUS 2264.description: Group percussion lessons for beginners or for students at an early stage of development. May be repeated for 1 credit. Consent required.

MUS 2274.title: Music Education Lab Ensemble
MUS 2274.description: Music education laboratory ensemble. Performance techniques, teaching methods, management procedures, materials and literature for school music ensembles. May be repeated for credit.

MUS 2284.title: Piano Accompanying
MUS 2284.description: Examine and practice the skills necessary for successful piano accompanying. Develop keyboard skills such as sightreading, transposition, choral score reading, and harmonization. Learn principles of accompanying vocal repertoire, instrumental repertoire, including large ensemble repertoire; adapt orchestral reductions for piano. Instructor consent required.

MUS 2314.title: Woodwind Techniques I - Flute, Clarinet, Saxophone
MUS 2314.description: Instruction in basic performing skills and practices for woodwind instruments (flute, clarinets, saxophone). Study of pedagogy for woodwind instruction in K-12 music education settings. Survey of repertoire, resources, and materials for use in woodwind instruction.

MUS 2324.title: Woodwind Techniques II - Oboe and Bassoon
MUS 2324.description: Instruction in basic performing skills and practices for woodwind instruments (oboe, bassoon). Study of pedagogy for woodwind instruction in K-12 music education settings. Survey of repertoire, resources, and materials for use in woodwind instruction.

MUS 2334.title: High Brass Techniques
MUS 2334.description: Instruction in basic performing skills and practices for high brass instruments (trumpet and horn). Study of pedagogy for teaching brass in K-12 music education settings. Survey of repertoire, resources, and materials for use in brass instruction.

MUS 2344.title: Low Brass Techniques
MUS 2344.description: Instruction in basic performing skills and practices for low brass instruments (trombone, euphonium, and tuba). Study of pedagogy for teaching brass in K-12 music education settings. Survey of repertoire, resources, and materials for use in brass instruction.

MUS 2364.title: Introduction to Music Education
MUS 2364.description: Principles and practices fundamental to music learning and teaching. Philosophical bases for teaching music. Major educational learning theories (e.g., behaviorism, cognitivism, social constructivism, multiple intelligences, spiral learning theory, Bloom’s taxonomy, etc.). Pedagogical approaches, culturally responsive teaching, and technology integration in the music classroom. Field observation for real world public-school music instruction.

MUS 2514.title: Individual Applied Voice
MUS 2514.description: Individual instruction in voice. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2515.title: Vocal Diction
MUS 2515.description: An introduction to principles of vocal diction for singing using the International Phonetic Alphabet and standard foreign-language pronunciation techniques.

MUS 2516.title: Vocal Diction
MUS 2516.description: An introduction to principles of vocal diction for singing using the International Phonetic Alphabet and standard foreign-language pronunciation techniques.

MUS 2524.title: Individual Applied Keyboard
MUS 2524.description: Individual instruction in keyboard. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2534.title: Individual Applied Violin
MUS 2534.description: Individual instruction in violin. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2544.title: Individual Applied Viola
MUS 2544.description: Individual instruction in viola. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2554.title: Individual Applied Cello
MUS 2554.description: Individual instruction in cello. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2564.title: Individual Applied Bass
MUS 2564.description: Individual instruction in bass. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2574.title: Individual Applied Flute
MUS 2574.description: Individual instruction in flute. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2584.title: Individual Applied Oboe
MUS 2584.description: Individual instruction in oboe. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2594.title: Individual Applied Clarinet
MUS 2594.description: Individual instruction in clarinet. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2604.title: Introduction to Arts Marketing
MUS 2604.description: An introduction to the theories and practice of marketing and building community engagement as applied to arts activities and professional not-for-profit arts organizations, through a survey of standard marketing approaches, examination of current practices in the field, and direct hands-on experience.

MUS 2614.title: Individual Applied Saxophone
MUS 2614.description: Individual instruction in saxophone. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2624.title: Individual Applied Bassoon
MUS 2624.description: Individual instruction in bassoon. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2634.title: Individual Applied Horn
MUS 2634.description: Individual instruction in horn. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2644.title: Individual Applied Trumpet
MUS 2644.description: Individual instruction in trumpet. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2654.title: Individual Applied Trombone
MUS 2654.description: Individual instruction in trombone. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2664.title: Individual Applied Baritone
MUS 2664.description: Individual instruction in baritone. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2674.title: Individual Applied Tuba
MUS 2674.description: Individual instruction in tuba. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2684.title: Individual Applied Percussion
MUS 2684.description: Individual instruction in percussion. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2694.title: Individual Applied Guitar
MUS 2694.description: Individual instruction in guitar to develop technical proficiency, musicality, and artistic expression. Emphasis placed on performance practice, sight-reading, improvisation, and interpretation. May be repeated 3 times with different content for a total of 9 credits. Pre: Audition required.

MUS 2734.title: Individual Applied Composition
MUS 2734.description: Individual instruction in composition. May be repeated. Consent and audition required.

MUS 2754.title: Individual Applied Recording
MUS 2754.description: Individual instruction through directed experiential learning of music recording and production. Integration of critical listening, acoustics, audio recording, and signal processing with music theory and performance. An emphasis on hands-on exploratory research in the use of instruments, acoustics, and microphone techniques combined with traditional methods and emerging technologies to capture and produce recordings of musical performances and works in a natural and effective manner. Permission required. May be repeated for a maximum of 8 hours.

MUS 2774.title: Individual Applied Harp
MUS 2774.description: Individual instruction in harp to develop technical proficiency, musicality, and artistic expression. Emphasis placed on performance practice, sight-reading, improvisation, and interpretation. May be repeated 3 times for a total of 9 credits. Pre: Audition required.

MUS 2815.title: Jazz Improvisation
MUS 2815.description: Fundamental principles of jazz improvisation. Topics include interval relationships, chord identification, modes and modality, blues and ii-V-I chord progressions. Pre: Permission of instructor required.

MUS 2816.title: Jazz Improvisation
MUS 2816.description: Fundamental principles of jazz improvisation. Topics include interval relationships, chord identification, modes and modality, blues and ii-V-I chord progressions. Pre: Permission of instructor required.

MUS 3024.title: Counterpoint
MUS 3024.description: Study of the development and aesthetics of contrapuntal techniques throughout the common practice period.

MUS 3025.title: European-American Music Analysis
MUS 3025.description: Extended compositional techniques in late-nineteenth and twentieth-century music, and analysis of larger works. 3025: chromatic harmony, twentieth-century techniques of pitch organization (e.g., set theory), grouping and displacement dissonance, large-scale musical forms. Analysis complemented by model composition and performance to demonstrate mastery of theoretical concepts and stylistic competency. 3026: synthesis of analytical techniques while navigating musical ambiguity in complete works of various sizes (miniatures to multi-part). Analytical observations connected to expressive or narrative meaning in musics from various styles and genres. Refine ability to write about music through research project.

MUS 3026.title: European-American Music Analysis
MUS 3026.description: Extended compositional techniques in late-nineteenth and twentieth-century music, and analysis of larger works. 3025: chromatic harmony, twentieth-century techniques of pitch organization (e.g., set theory), grouping and displacement dissonance, large-scale musical forms. Analysis complemented by model composition and performance to demonstrate mastery of theoretical concepts and stylistic competency. 3026: synthesis of analytical techniques while navigating musical ambiguity in complete works of various sizes (miniatures to multi-part). Analytical observations connected to expressive or narrative meaning in musics from various styles and genres. Refine ability to write about music through research project.

MUS 3034.title: Form and Analysis in the Common-practice Period
MUS 3034.description: Domains of rhythm and meter, harmony, and cadence as related to musical form. Score-based and aural analysis of formal functions of common theme-types and large-scale forms in selected works from the mid-eighteenth through nineteenth centuries using William Caplin’s theory. Identification of deviations from stylistic norms. Analysis complemented by model composition to demonstrate mastery of theoretical concepts and stylistic competency.

MUS 3035.title: Advanced Class Piano
MUS 3035.description: Develop keyboard skills such as sightreading, harmonization, transposition, learn all scales/arpeggios and important keyboard progressions. A grade of C or better required in prerequisite.

MUS 3036.title: Advanced Class Piano
MUS 3036.description: Continued development of keyboard skills. Advanced transposition, harmonization, and sightreading, open score reading, and real-world application of skills acquired throughout keyboard study. A grade of C or better required in prerequisite.

MUS 3044.title: Orchestration & Analysis
MUS 3044.description: An introduction to the craft of scoring and arranging of music for full orchestra. Analysis of scores, small projects and a full orchestration project.

MUS 3045.title: Advanced Ear Training
MUS 3045.description: 3045: Hearing chromatic chord function in melodic and harmonic contexts. Sight-singing chromatic melodies and performing chromatic progressions. Aurally recognizing musical form (binary, ternary, strophic). Discovering markedness in common practice era music and recognizing commonalities with and differences from other music cultures A grade of C or better required in prerequisite. 3046: Hearing chord function in advanced chromatic melodic and harmonic contexts. Sight-singing advanced chromatic melodies and performing highly chromatic progressions. Aurally recognizing musical form (sonata, rondo, other forms). Hypothesizing about evolution of style and articulating intertextual experience. A grade of C or better required in prerequisite.

MUS 3054.title: Introduction to Vocal/choral Arranging
MUS 3054.description: Techniques of arranging music for vocal/choral ensembles. Emphasis on transcription from recordings to develop rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic dictation skills. Discussion, transcription, listening, small writing exercises, final project.

MUS 3056.title: Music and Media Production
MUS 3056.description: Develops advanced knowledge of music production through practical application of music recording and production technologies, including advanced microphone techniques, critical listening, and critical artistic evaluation skills. Individual and group production projects. Hands-on experience with a variety if expressive media technologies including CD and DVD production in a collaborative, interdisciplinary team approach.

MUS 3064.title: Digital Sound Manipulation
MUS 3064.description: Cross-disciplinary study of recording technology and its effects on music. Aesthetics of electronic music. Recording and editing digital sound. Visual programming for live sound synthesis and processing. Acoustic compilers for programmatic sound processing and synthesis. Individual creative applications of tools learned in class. Team-based work on creative projects. Emphasis on intercultural and global use of creative music technologies.

MUS 3065.title: Computer Music and Multimedia Design
MUS 3065.description: A two-semester study of interactive multimedia composition and performance software as a foundation for creative work and research endeavors. Also provides an in-depth study of digital sound synthesis, algorithmic creation of multimedia content, and the design of audio-visual interactive systems using latest technologies. Must meet pre-requisite or have permission of the instructor

MUS 3066.title: Computer Music and Multimedia Design
MUS 3066.description: A two-semester study of interactive multimedia composition and performance software as a foundation for creative work and research endeavors. Also provides an in-depth study of digital sound synthesis, algorithmic creation of multimedia content, and the design of audio-visual interactive systems using latest technologies. Must meet pre-requisite or have permission of the instructor

MUS 3074.title: Topics in Music Analysis
MUS 3074.description: Contemporary methods of music analysis. Readings from landmark music theory texts and top music theory journals. Analysis of complementary music. Formulating unique research projects to demonstrate mastery of theoretical frameworks. May be repeated 2 times with different content for a maximum of 9 credit hours.

MUS 3114.title: Symphonic Literature
MUS 3114.description: Study of representative works of symphonic music from the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries, with corollary readings in the history of musical ideas. Consent required.

MUS 3124.title: 20th Century Music Literature
MUS 3124.description: An introduction to music in Europe and America since 1945; supplementary study in the aesthetics of contemporary music. Consent required.

MUS 3134.title: Vocal Music Literature
MUS 3134.description: Covers vocal music of Europe and America, especially music composed the eighteenth century. Examines differences in style and forms of choral and solo-vocal expression characteristic of the Baroque, Classic, Romantic, and Modern eras. Discusses issues of vocal performance practice. Ability to read music required.

MUS 3144.title: Early Music Literature
MUS 3144.description: Covers vocal and instrumental music from the Middle Ages to the eighteenth century. Examines differences in style and forms of expression characteristic especially of Medieval, Renaissance, and early Baroque music. Discusses issues of performance practice. Ability to read music required.

MUS 3164.title: History of Electronic Music
MUS 3164.description: Seminal electronic music works in historical context. Electronic music practices of the 20th and 21st centuries. The technologies of electronic music. Analysis of electronic music. Historical origins and trends in electronic music. Connections between experimental and popular electronic music forms.

MUS 3164H.title: History of Electronic Music
MUS 3164H.description: Seminal electronic music works in historical context. Electronic music practices of the 20th and 21st centuries. The technologies of electronic music. Analysis of electronic music. Historical origins and trends in electronic music. Connections between experimental and popular electronic music forms.

MUS 3174.title: Music as Global Culture
MUS 3174.description: Musical traditions from around the globe as both artistic production and cultural practice. Expose students to music from both non-Western and Western traditions. Connect cultural context to musical meaning. Critical engagement with different musics and their histories.

MUS 3184.title: Histories of Music I: Music in the European and American Traditions
MUS 3184.description: Examination of the development of different musical genres in Europe and the Americas from approximately 1600 to 1918. Consideration of historical and sociocultural context. Introduction of a diverse array of styles and genres. Critical engagement with social, cultural, and historical issues and their relation to music. Development of historical research skills, facility with writing about music, and practical applications.

MUS 3194.title: Histories of Music II: Music in the 20th and 21st Centuries
MUS 3194.description: Musical traditions and developments in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, with emphasis on music (voice, acoustic, and electronic) in the United States and increasing globalization. Introduction of students to music from both non-Western and Western traditions. Critical engagement with formalized and vernacular musics through sociopolitical concepts (race, gender, etc.). Research into music in the twenty-first century United States. Development of both historical and ethnographic research skills. Writing about music.

MUS 3214.title: Teaching Music in the Elementary School
MUS 3214.description: Methods of teaching elementary school music. Emphasis on Kodaly, Orff, and traditional music textbook series approaches to teaching music in elementary schools. Pre: Instructor permission and successful completion of sophomore music continuation exam.

MUS 3225.title: Conducting
MUS 3225.description: An introduction to the practice and theory of ensemble conducting and leadership. 3225: Basic conducting skills, and choral conducting. 3226: Intermediate conducting skills, and instrumental conducting. Consent required.

MUS 3226.title: Conducting
MUS 3226.description: An introduction to the practice and theory of ensemble conducting and leadership. 3225: Basic conducting skills, and choral conducting. 3226: Intermediate conducting skills, and instrumental conducting. Consent required.

MUS 3234.title: Piano Pedagogy
MUS 3234.description: Examination of principles and practice of piano pedagogy. Covers teaching methods, materials and literature for the independent studio teacher. Pre: consent required.

MUS 3244.title: Vocal Pedagogy
MUS 3244.description: Exploration of historical and modern treatises. Implementation of technical methods to build vocal technique. Experimentation with biofeedback in pedagogical context. Practical application of pedagogical methods. Pre: Successful completion of continuation exam.

MUS 3314.title: Instrumental Ensemble Music
MUS 3314.description: Instruction and participation in instrumental music performance ensembles under direction of members of the music faculty. Attention to technical proficiency, stylistic elements, musical design and interpretation in the works to be performed. Addresses ethical obligations and practice in a music ensemble setting. May be repeated for a combined maximum of 8 hours. Consent and audition required.

MUS 3414.title: Choral Ensemble Music
MUS 3414.description: Instruction and participation in choral music performance ensembles under direction of members of the music faculty. Attention to technical proficiency, stylistic elements, musical design and interpretation in the works to be performed. Addresses ethical obligations and practice in a music ensemble setting. May be repeated for a combined maximum of 8 hours. Consent and audition required.

MUS 3814.title: Jazz History
MUS 3814.description: A survey and analysis of jazz music, including traditional jazz, big band, bebop, rhythm and blues, free jazz/avant garde, fusion, and hip-hop. Exploration of historical, social, and cultural forces and trends that influence the creation and interpretation of jazz music.

MUS 3815.title: Advanced Jazz Improvisation
MUS 3815.description: Topics will include in-depth analysis of the great improvisers in multiple genres with a focus on developing professional-level skills.

MUS 3900.title: Bridge Experience
MUS 3900.description: Application of academic knowledge and skills to in a work-based experience aligned with post-graduation goals using research-based learning processes. Satisfactory completion of work-based experience often in the form of internship, undergraduate research, co-op, or study abroad; self-evaluation; reflection; and showcase of learning. Pre: Departmental approval of 3900 plan.

MUS 4014.title: Topics in Advanced Electroacoustic Research
MUS 4014.description: Rotating advanced research topics in electroacoustic music. Sonification, spatialization, algorithmic music, electronic music instrument design, digital performance ensembles, and advanced computer music composition. Repeatable with different content up to a maximum of 12 credit hours.

MUS 4014H.title: Topics Adv Electroacoustic Res
MUS 4014H.description: Rotating advanced research topics in electroacoustic music. Sonification, spatialization, algorithmic music, electronic music instrument design, digital performance ensembles, and advanced computer music composition. Repeatable with different content up to a maximum of 12 credit hours.

MUS 4055.title: Music Technology Senior Seminar
MUS 4055.description: Weekly seminars in music technology with group discussion of progress in current student projects, the current state of artistic and business practices in the recording industry, and guest lecturers drawn from the professional world.

MUS 4056.title: Music Technology Senior Seminar
MUS 4056.description: Weekly seminars in music technology with group discussion of progress in current student projects, the current state of artistic and business practices in the recording industry, and guest lecturers drawn from the professional world.

MUS 4124.title: Special Topics in Music History and Literature
MUS 4124.description: Specific, in depth study of one of several topics in music history and or literature.

MUS 4174.title: Topics in Musicology
MUS 4174.description: Examine topics in historical musicology and their interdisciplinary resonance. Examination of primary sources, top musicology journals, and monographs as appropriate. Historical and technical analysis of music. Investigation of historical and sociocultural context of music. May be repeated 2 times with different content for a maximum of 9 credit hours.

MUS 4204.title: Secondary General and Choral Music Education Methods
MUS 4204.description: This course examines philosophical, planning, administrative, organizational, instructional methods, assessment of student learning and cultural performances necessary to manage and teach secondary general and choral music programs.

MUS 4214.title: Instrumental Methods: Elementary
MUS 4214.description: Develop skills and practices to direct an elementary instrumental music program in a school setting. Learn practices, procedures, and strategies for leading rehearsals and lessons, developing curriculum, assessing student learning, and administering a school instrumental program.

MUS 4224.title: Instrumental Methods: Secondary
MUS 4224.description: Develop skills and practices to direct an instrumental music program in a middle or high school setting. Learn practices, procedures, and strategies for leading rehearsals and lessons, developing curriculum, assessing student learning, and administering a school instrumental music program.

MUS 4234.title: Topics in Music Education
MUS 4234.description: Study of specialized areas of pedagogy, instruction, administration, and classroom management in music education. Prepares students to lead specialized ensembles and courses in school music contexts. Course can only be taken one time for credit toward degree requirements.

MUS 4694.title: Advanced Individual Applied Guitar
MUS 4694.description: Individualized instruction for advanced guitar students focusing on the continued development of technical mastery, musical interpretation, and artistic expression. Engage with a broad repertoire spanning multiple genres and historical periods, including solo, ensemble, and improvisational works. Emphasis on refining tone production, advanced techniques, phrasing, and stylistic authenticity. Work toward professional-level recital preparation, audition readiness, and deepening interpretative insight. Regular performance opportunities, juries, and goal-setting are integral components of the course. May be repeated 3 times for a total of 8 credits. Pre: Music Majors or Minors only. Performance continuation exam required.

MUS 4734.description: Individual instruction in composition at an advanced level. Majors only. May be repeated. Performance continuation exam required.

MUS 4744.title: Advanced Individual Applied Conducting
MUS 4744.description: Individual instruction in conducting at an advanced level. May be repeated. Consent required.

MUS 4754.title: Advanced Individual Applied Recording
MUS 4754.description: Individual instruction through directed experiential learning in music recording and production at an advanced level. Integration of critical listening, acoustics, audio recording, signal processing, audio mixing, and audio mastering with music theory and performance. An emphasis in hands-on exploratory research in the use of instruments, acoustics, microphones, recording, and production techniques combined with traditional methods and emerging technologies to capture and produce recordings in an artistic manner suitable for use in a senior portfolio. Permission required. May be repeated for a maximum of 12 hours.

MUS 4764.title: Advanced Individual Applied Electroacoustics
MUS 4764.description: Individual instruction and completion of a major project in electroacoustic composition, performance, or research, at an advanced level. Repeatable up to three times for a maximum of 3 credit hours.

MUS 4774.title: Advanced Individual Applied Harp
MUS 4774.description: Individualized instruction for advanced harp students focusing on the continued development of technical proficiency, musical interpretation, and artistic expression. Engage with a diverse repertoire spanning various historical periods and styles, including solo, chamber, and orchestral works. Emphasis on refining tone production, advanced finger techniques, phrasing, and performance practice. Work toward developing professional-level recital preparation, audition readiness, and interpretative depth. Regular performance opportunities, juries, and goal-setting are integral components of the course. May be repeated 3 times for a total of 8 credits. Pre: Music Majors or Minors only. Performance continuation exam required.
